tridoshic.name: Tridoshic
tridoshic.summary: Your answers spread almost evenly across Vata, Pitta and Kapha. In Ayurveda this is called a tridoshic constitution: no single dosha runs the show, so the question is less "which one am I" and more "which one is out of balance this season". Read the dosha below as the one currently leading, not as a fixed type.
tridoshic.readingAs: Reading {{dosha}} as the one leading today

dream.title: Dream interpreter
dream.intro: Describe your dream in as much detail as you remember. Don’t worry about order or clarity — the mind works in symbols. We’ll match archetypal patterns and offer reflective questions to sit with. Dreams don’t have single meanings; they have invitations.
dream.label: Tell me about your dream
dream.placeholder: I was standing by a dark ocean and couldn’t find my way home. A bird flew overhead carrying something in its beak…
dream.privacy: Your dream text is sent to the interpretation service and is not stored server-side. If offline, we fall back to a local symbol dictionary.
dream.needLonger: Please share a bit more about the dream (at least a few sentences).
dream.noMatch: No immediately common archetypes surfaced in this dream text — but that doesn’t mean it’s silent. Often the most personal dreams use symbols unique to your life. Sit with the strongest image from the dream. Ask: what is it the opposite of? What in my life does it rhyme with?
dream.practiceBody: Keep a notebook by your bed. Record dreams the moment you wake, before they fade. Over time, recurring symbols reveal the language your unconscious uses with you.
dream.genericReflection: Dreams bring messages — honour the question they leave with you.
dream.compensatoryLabel: What your waking self is missing
dream.compensatoryHint: Jung: dreams compensate for the conscious attitude. This is what the dream offers that you don’t already have.
dream.aiFallback: The interpretation service didn’t answer, so this reading comes from the symbol dictionary instead. No Moonstones were taken.

dark-triad.title: Dark Triad shadow
dark-triad.description: Three shadow traits psychologists call the 'dark triad' — narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy — exist to some degree in all of us. Surface where your shadow runs strongest.
whatYouGet: Healthy and shadow forms of each

n1.text: I tend to feel I deserve special treatment.

n2.text: I like being the center of attention.

n3.text: I expect to be recognised as exceptional.

n4.text: I believe I am more talented than most people.

n5.text: I sometimes think the rules don’t apply to me.

m1.text: I use flattery to get what I want from people.

m2.text: I keep my real motives private when dealing with others.

m3.text: I manipulate conversations to land where I want them to.

m4.text: I tell people what they want to hear if it gets me what I need.

m5.text: I believe most people can be bought at some price.

p1.text: I don’t worry much about other people’s feelings.

p2.text: I take risks that most people would call reckless.

p3.text: Consequences don’t hold me back the way they hold others back.

p4.text: I stay unmoved when someone cries in front of me.

p5.text: I find rules of conduct often arbitrary and ignorable.

narcissism.name: Narcissistic Shadow
narcissism.tagline: The hungry self — craves mirroring, fears insignificance.
narcissism.summary: Your shadow is strongest around narcissism — the hunger to be seen, admired, special. This energy built whole empires and whole disasters. In its healthy form it is confidence, charisma, the courage to take up space. In its shadow it is a bottomless mirror that cannot be filled.
shadow: Believing rules don’t apply to you
narcissism.affirmation: I take up my space — and I let others be as bright as I am.

machiavellianism.name: Machiavellian Shadow
machiavellianism.tagline: The strategist — sees the game, plays several moves ahead.
machiavellianism.summary: Your shadow leans toward strategy — reading the room, steering conversations, playing the long game. At its best this is wisdom and political skill. In shadow it corrodes intimacy: you stop trusting anyone to just be with you, because you are always several moves ahead.
shadow: Inability to be present — always calculating
machiavellianism.affirmation: I see the game — and I know when to put the chessboard down.

psychopathy.name: Psychopathic Shadow
psychopathy.tagline: The cold one — unencumbered by fear, unencumbered by bond.
psychopathy.summary: Your shadow runs coldest — low fear, low attachment, high willingness to break rules. The healthy version is the surgeon who does not freeze, the soldier who protects, the CEO who makes the hard call. In shadow, it is disconnection — the freezing of warmth that would have sustained you.
shadow: Coldness where connection is asked for
psychopathy.affirmation: I have the cold — and I choose when to let warmth back in.

low.name: Low shadow signal
low.summary: You endorsed little of any of the three traits, so the mirror is quiet today. That is not a verdict of sainthood: everyone carries some of each, and a low reading can also mean you answered as you would like to be rather than as you are. Come back on a harder day and see what shows.
shadow: A quiet mirror can also be a flattering one
An edge you under-rate is an edge you never examine
low.affirmation: I look at my shadow without flinching, even when it is faint.

disc.title: DISC behavioural profile
disc.description: A four-quadrant model of workplace behaviour: Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, Conscientiousness. See which style leads for you and how you naturally contribute to a team.
whatYouGet: How to collaborate with other styles

d1.text: I move fast and push past obstacles.

d2.text: I like to lead rather than follow.

d3.text: I’m direct, even blunt, when the stakes are high.

d4.text: I make decisions quickly and push them through.

d5.text: I’d rather act now and adjust later.

i1.text: I love being around people and feed off their energy.

i2.text: I persuade easily with warmth and enthusiasm.

i4.text: I make friends wherever I go.

i5.text: I would rather win people over than instruct them.

s1.text: I value stability and long-term relationships.

s2.text: I’m a patient listener who remembers details about people.

s4.text: I resolve conflict by finding middle ground.

c1.text: I prioritise accuracy and getting the details right.

c3.text: I ask clarifying questions before committing.

c4.text: I follow procedures even when they feel slow.

dominance.name: Dominance (D)
dominance.summary: You lead by moving. You set direction, break through barriers, and thrive on challenge. People trust you to make the call when a call is needed.
dominance.affirmation: I move with force — and I remember the people moving with me.

influence.name: Influence (I)
influence.summary: You lead by connecting. Your energy is contagious. You inspire, build coalitions, and keep morale up through rough stretches.
influence.affirmation: My warmth is my lever — and I use it even in the hard conversations.

steadiness.name: Steadiness (S)
steadiness.summary: You lead by staying. Teams rely on your consistency. You’re the person who remembers what happened last time, who settles conflicts, who keeps the ship upright through storms.
steadiness.affirmation: I am the calm — and I speak up when speaking up is needed.

conscientiousness.name: Conscientiousness (C)
conscientiousness.summary: You lead by thinking. Your standards are high. You catch errors others miss, build systems that don’t fall apart, and make sure the work actually works.
conscientiousness.affirmation: My rigour protects the work — and I ship at 85% when 85% is right.

money-personality.title: Money personality
money-personality.description: Five distinct patterns of relating to money — the Saver, the Spender, the Avoider, the Monk, the Status-Seeker. See which script your money self is running.
whatYouGet: When it serves you and when it doesn’t

sv1.text: I feel most at peace when my savings account is growing.

sv2.text: I’d rather skip a purchase I want than tap into savings.

sp1.text: If something will make today better, I buy it.

sp2.text: If I can afford it now, I buy it now.

sp3.text: Money is meant to be enjoyed, not hoarded.

av1.text: Checking my bank balance makes me anxious.

av2.text: I let bills and statements pile up unopened.

av3.text: I could not say, even roughly, how much money I have right now.

mk1.text: I feel conflicted about having more money than others.

mk2.text: I feel uneasy about wanting more money than I need.

st1.text: I use what I buy to signal what kind of person I am.

st2.text: How I look to others shapes my spending.

st3.text: I’d rather have the nicer option even if I strain the budget.

saver.name: The Saver
saver.summary: You feel safest when the cushion is growing. Savings aren’t just numbers — they’re proof you’re okay. This gives you discipline and long-horizon thinking most people lack.
strengths: Low financial anxiety when the cushion is fed
saver.affirmation: I build the cushion — and I live fully in the present it protects.

spender.name: The Spender
spender.summary: Money is for living. You invest in experiences, share generously, and refuse to treat your one life as a retirement spreadsheet. The trade-off: financial margin can run thin.
strengths: Willingness to invest in experiences and growth
shadow: Impulse buys that don’t actually bring joy
spender.affirmation: I invest in life — and I build a foundation so the life keeps going.

avoider.name: The Avoider
avoider.tagline: Head in the sand — money is a thing that happens to you.
avoider.summary: Money stresses you, so you don’t look. Bills pile up, numbers blur, fear builds. This is usually learned — a response to scarcity or chaos earlier in life. It is workable.
shadow: Anxiety that grows because it isn’t faced
avoider.affirmation: I open the envelope. I face the number. What I look at stops running me.

monk.name: The Monk
monk.tagline: Ethical conflict with wealth — "money is compromised".
monk.summary: You have a moral/spiritual tension with money. This can be real wisdom — you’re onto something about what money does to people. But it can also be a convenient script that stops you from ever having any.
shadow: Believing wealth and ethics are incompatible
Financial anxiety under a spiritual-sounding cover
monk.affirmation: I can be ethical and financially safe. Both / and.

status.name: The Status-Seeker
status.tagline: Uses money to signal identity and belonging.
status.summary: What you buy says something about who you are. At best this is aesthetic intelligence and social savvy. At worst, it is a treadmill that never stops — someone else always has more.
shadow: Spending on image rather than enjoyment
Debt from projecting what you don’t have
status.affirmation: I like beautiful things — and I no longer need them to prove who I am.

boundaries.title: Boundaries check-in
boundaries.description: Where are your boundaries strong, where are they weak, and where do they shift depending on who’s asking? Four patterns: rigid walls, porous openness, healthy flex, situation-dependent.
whatYouGet: Where your boundaries are firm, porous, or situational

rg1.text: I keep people at arm’s length even when I’d like to be closer.

rg2.text: I find it hard to ask for help.

rg3.text: I rarely share my emotions with anyone.

rg4.text: I have strict rules about who gets access to me.

po1.text: I take on other people’s problems as if they were my own.

po2.text: I find it hard to say no to a request.

po4.text: My mood depends heavily on how others feel about me.

hl1.text: I say no when I need to, without a long explanation.

hl2.text: I can support someone without absorbing their distress.

hl3.text: I share personal things at a pace that matches the relationship.

hl4.text: I notice when someone crosses a line and address it.

sn1.text: My boundaries depend on how powerful the other person is.

sn2.text: I hold the line with strangers but cave with family.

sn3.text: I have totally different rules in work vs. personal life.

sn4.text: I fluctuate between too-open and too-closed depending on stress.

rigid.name: Rigid Walls
rigid.tagline: Protected — often over-protected — from being hurt.
rigid.summary: Your boundaries lean toward walls: firm, high, not often crossed. This means you don’t get hurt easily. It also means connection has to work hard to reach you. The work is learning which walls still serve and which ones locked you in.
shadow: Walls that stopped a past hurt but block present joy
rigid.affirmation: My boundaries protect me and allow the right people in. I choose which walls stay and which come down.

porous.name: Porous Openness
porous.tagline: Deeply open — often overwhelmed by what gets in.
porous.summary: Your boundaries are permeable. You absorb what others feel. You over-share. You have trouble saying no. This gift of openness is real — and it needs a skin, not a wall, around it.
shadow: Resentment from saying yes too often
porous.affirmation: I feel it all — and I choose what I take in. Yes and no are both love.

healthy.name: Healthy Flex
healthy.tagline: Firm enough to hold you, soft enough to let people in.
healthy.summary: Your boundaries know how to move. You can say no without guilt, yes without losing yourself, and you notice quickly when something is off. This is the target state — which does not mean the work is over, but it means you have the skills.
shadow: Holding healthy boundaries can exhaust you when around unhealthy ones
healthy.affirmation: My yes is a yes. My no is a no. Both are complete sentences.

situational.name: Situation-Dependent
situational.summary: Your boundaries shift by context. Strong at work, porous with family. Firm with strangers, collapsing with loved ones. This is workable — but the unpredictability is a clue: somewhere, a certain situation overrides your stated values. Identify it, meet it, and your boundaries become consistent.
shadow: Disowning a part of yourself in certain relationships
situational.affirmation: My values are the same everywhere. I find the places where I forget that — and I return.

burnout.title: Burnout check
burnout.description: Burnout has three measurable dimensions: exhaustion (drained energy), cynicism (distance from the work), and efficacy-loss (I’m not effective anymore). See where you are today.
whatYouGet: Exhaustion vs cynicism vs efficacy-loss profile
Which dimension needs your attention first

ex1.text: My work leaves me emotionally wrung out.

ex2.text: Mornings feel heavy because of what the day holds.

ex3.text: Getting through a full day takes everything I have.

ex4.text: By evening I have nothing left for anything else.

cy1.text: The work I once cared about has stopped mattering to me.

cy2.text: I have become more sceptical about whether my work makes any difference.

cy3.text: I would rather just get my tasks done and be left alone.

cy4.text: I question whether what I do has any real value.

ef1.text: I am getting less done than I used to, and it bothers me.

ef2.text: It feels like my efforts no longer lead anywhere.

ef3.text: I have lost confidence in my ability to do my job well.

ef4.text: I feel I have little control over how my work goes.

exhaustion.name: Exhaustion-Dominant Burnout
exhaustion.tagline: The tank is empty. Energy is the first thing to rebuild.
exhaustion.summary: Your burnout expresses as pure depletion. You can still see the value of your work, still care about the outcomes — you just don’t have the energy left to deliver. This is the most reversible form of burnout if caught here.
strengths: You haven’t disconnected from your values yet
shadow: Pushing through will make it worse
Sleep and rest no longer refill you the way they used to
exhaustion.affirmation: My body has given me a signal. I listen to it. Rest is the work right now.

cynicism.name: Cynicism-Dominant Burnout
cynicism.tagline: You’ve detached. The work stopped mattering.
cynicism.summary: Your burnout is in your relationship to the work itself. You still have some energy, but you’ve emotionally checked out. The fire went out. Doing the work feels hollow. This is a warning sign — the longer cynicism sits, the harder it is to reconnect.
strengths: You can see clearly what is broken — cynicism is often accurate observation
shadow: Numbness seeping into other parts of your life
Sarcasm where care used to live
cynicism.affirmation: My cynicism is real information. It’s telling me something I can’t ignore any longer.

efficacy-loss.name: Efficacy-Loss Burnout
efficacy-loss.summary: Your burnout shows up as questioning whether you’re any good at this anymore. This is the most painful form because it attacks self-concept. It also has the most compact fix: wins. Not "prove yourself" wins — small visible completions that remind you you can still finish things.
shadow: Avoiding challenging work because you fear failing
Deep loneliness — you don’t tell anyone you feel this way
efficacy-loss.affirmation: I remember what I’ve done. I take one win today, real and visible, and I let it count.

low.name: Running warm, not burnt out
low.tagline: None of the three dimensions is elevated.
low.summary: None of the three dimensions is elevated: you still have energy for the day, the work still means something, and you still trust yourself to do it. Keep the habits that are working — rest, boundaries, a sense of why — because burnout arrives slowly and leaves slowly.
strengths: The work still matters to you
shadow: Low today is not low forever — check in again in a month
A good reading can tempt you to skip the rest that produced it
low.affirmation: I protect what is working before anything breaks.

communication.title: Communication style
communication.description: Four styles emerge under difficulty: passive (hide), aggressive (attack), passive-aggressive (sideways), assertive (clear + respectful). See your default and which is available when you’re regulated.
whatYouGet: A practice for the hard conversations

ps1.text: I stay silent even when I disagree, to avoid conflict.

ps2.text: I apologise for things that weren’t my fault.

ps3.text: I let others make decisions for me to keep the peace.

ag1.text: I raise my voice when I feel crossed.

ag2.text: I interrupt others to make my point.

ag3.text: I use biting remarks or sarcasm to win arguments.

pa1.text: I say "I’m fine" when I’m not.

pa2.text: I use the silent treatment to signal displeasure.

pa3.text: I forget or delay things on purpose when I’m resentful.

as1.text: I state what I want directly, without apologising for wanting it.

as2.text: I listen fully before responding, even when I disagree.

as3.text: I can say no firmly while staying warm.

passive.name: Passive
passive.tagline: Silence over safety — your needs come last.
passive.summary: Your default is to keep the peace by keeping quiet. This often develops in environments where speaking up had bad consequences. Short-term, it reduces conflict. Long-term, it builds resentment and disconnects you from what you actually want.
shadow: Your real self stops showing up
Others never learn what you actually want
passive.affirmation: My needs matter as much as anyone else’s. I practice saying them out loud.

aggressive.name: Aggressive
aggressive.tagline: Force first — my needs override yours.
aggressive.summary: You push. You raise your voice. You override others to get where you need to go. This gets results in some settings (and fails badly in others). Under the force is usually fear that if you don’t push you’ll be overrun.
strengths: Direct — people know where they stand
aggressive.affirmation: My power is real — and I wield it precisely. I don’t need to overpower to be heard.

passive-aggressive.name: Passive-Aggressive
passive-aggressive.tagline: Indirect resistance — saying no with my actions.
passive-aggressive.summary: You can’t (or don’t) say what you’re feeling directly — so it comes out sideways. The silent treatment, "forgetting", veiled comments. This is the most corrosive style because the other person senses the hostility but can’t address it.
strengths: Sensitivity to environments where directness is punished
shadow: Nobody around you knows what’s wrong
You don’t fully admit the anger even to yourself
passive-aggressive.affirmation: My anger is clean information. I say it directly — or I let it go.

assertive.name: Assertive
assertive.tagline: Clear and respectful — my needs and yours, both.
assertive.summary: You say what you mean. You listen before you respond. You can say no without apologising and yes without dissolving. This is the target state — and it is a practice, not a personality. Notice which situations pull you out of it.
shadow: Can occasionally slip to aggressive under threat, or passive with specific people
assertive.affirmation: I stand in my truth and honour yours. Both can be real at once.

conflict.title: Conflict style
conflict.description: The Thomas-Kilmann model identifies five modes for handling conflict: competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating. See your preferred response — and which modes you need to practice.

cp1.text: I argue hard for what I think is right.

cp2.text: I’d rather win than keep the peace.

cp3.text: I make strong cases and don’t back down easily.

cl1.text: I work to find solutions that meet everyone’s needs.

cl2.text: I dig into the real problem behind the surface disagreement.

cl3.text: I keep talking until we find something that works for both of us.

cm1.text: I’m quick to offer a compromise to settle things.

cm2.text: I think meeting halfway is usually fair.

cm3.text: I’d rather both of us get partial wins than fight for total.

av1.text: I avoid people I’m in conflict with until the tension fades.

av2.text: I don’t bring up issues that might cause friction.

av3.text: I hope disagreements resolve themselves over time.

ac1.text: I give in to keep the relationship intact.

ac2.text: I let others have their way when they feel strongly.

ac3.text: I find it hard to put my needs above someone else’s.

competing.name: Competing
competing.tagline: Assertive, uncooperative — fights for own position.
competing.summary: Your default mode is to fight for what you believe is right. Great when the stakes are high and you have the right answer. Dangerous when it’s low-stakes or you don’t actually have the right answer.
shadow: Blind spots about your own fallibility
competing.affirmation: I fight when it matters — and I lay down the sword most of the time.

collaborating.name: Collaborating
collaborating.tagline: Assertive + cooperative — works for both to win.
collaborating.summary: You dig into the real problem and look for solutions that satisfy everyone. This is usually the best mode when relationships matter and time allows. It does cost — time, patience, emotional labour.
collaborating.affirmation: I work for solutions that serve everyone — and I know when to move faster.

compromising.name: Compromising
compromising.tagline: Moderately assertive + cooperative — meet in the middle.
compromising.summary: You look for the midpoint. This is pragmatic, faster than full collaboration, and keeps relationships workable. The risk: both sides feel a little robbed, and the real problem underneath stays unaddressed.
compromising.affirmation: I find workable middles — and I dig deeper when middle isn’t good enough.

avoiding.name: Avoiding
avoiding.summary: You prefer to not engage. This is right when the issue is minor, the relationship matters more than the issue, or you need time. It’s wrong when the avoided thing is actually important — it compounds underneath.
strengths: Wisdom about which fights to avoid
shadow: Relationships slowly corrode from un-addressed issues
avoiding.affirmation: I choose my fights — and I name the ones that need naming, even when it’s uncomfortable.

accommodating.name: Accommodating
accommodating.tagline: Unassertive, cooperative — gives in to keep peace.
accommodating.summary: You tend to give in. For relationships or people you love, this is a real gift. It becomes a problem when it’s automatic — when you lose track of what you actually need.
shadow: Others never learn your real preferences
accommodating.affirmation: My giving is a choice, not a reflex. I check what I need before I yield.

chronotype.title: Sleep chronotype
chronotype.description: Dr. Michael Breus’ chronotype model identifies four sleep-wake personalities: the Lion (morning), the Bear (daytime), the Wolf (evening), and the Dolphin (restless). Sixteen questions reveal which rhythm is yours — and when your real peak hours are.
whatYouGet: Sleep + schedule tips that actually suit you

lo1.text: I wake up naturally before 6 AM feeling rested.

lo2.text: My most productive hours are 6-10 AM.

lo3.text: I fade fast in the evening and am usually asleep by 10 PM.

be1.text: I wake between 7 and 9 AM without trouble.

be2.text: My best hours are 10 AM to 2 PM.

be3.text: I hit a natural slump around 3-4 PM.

wo1.text: I struggle to wake before 8 AM no matter what time I slept.

wo2.text: My productive window doesn’t open until afternoon or evening.

wo3.text: I feel most alive late at night, past 10 PM.

wo4.text: Even after a full night’s sleep, I am slow and groggy for the first hours of the morning.

do1.text: I wake up multiple times a night even when tired.

do2.text: I have a sensitive nervous system — light, sound, thoughts wake me.

do3.text: I feel sleepy early in the evening, then wide awake again around 10 PM.

do4.text: I lie awake replaying the day even when I am exhausted.

lion.name: The Lion
lion.tagline: Early riser, peak morning, sunset energy.
lion.summary: You wake easily, get your best work done before noon, and fade by 9 PM. About 15% of people are lions. Your secret: build your hardest work into 6-10 AM, do maintenance work midday, and honour the early bedtime.
shadow: Can feel like an outsider in a night-owl culture
lion.affirmation: My early light is a gift. I schedule my life around when my lion hunts.

bear.name: The Bear
bear.tagline: Solar-rhythm — rises with the sun, peaks midday.
bear.summary: You follow the sun. Asleep by 11, up around 7-8, peak focus 10 AM-2 PM, natural dip 3-4 PM, fade by 10 PM. About 55% of people are bears. Most work and school schedules are built around this rhythm.
shadow: The 3-4 PM slump is real — honour it
Can drift into night-owl patterns under stress
bear.affirmation: My rhythm is steady. I ride the sun, rest when it dips, and sleep when it sets.

wolf.name: The Wolf
wolf.tagline: Late night predator — peak creative at 9 PM.
wolf.summary: You are biologically programmed to be at peak alertness late at night. Mornings punish you. About 15% of people are wolves. This is not a defect — your natural rhythm just clashes with school-and-office schedules.
strengths: Deep focus when the world is quiet
Night thinking different from day thinking
shadow: Social rhythm conflict with partners/kids on normal schedules
wolf.affirmation: My rhythm is not broken. I design the life I can design around it — and I negotiate the rest.

dolphin.name: The Dolphin
dolphin.summary: You sleep the way dolphins do — half-awake. Sensitive to light, sound, thoughts. Wake multiple times a night. Often labeled "insomniac". About 10% of people are dolphins. Breus describes dolphins as perceptive, detail-focused and often anxious. Routine is medicine.
dolphin.affirmation: My nervous system needs gentle ritual. I build a sleep practice and honour how sensitive I am.

creative-type.title: Creative type
creative-type.description: Five ways of being creative — five roles in the creative process. The Maker, the Dreamer, the Performer, the Organiser, the Analyser. See which you take on naturally — and who you partner best with.
whatYouGet: Your role in the creative process

mk1.text: I create with my hands — building, crafting, making tangibles.

mk2.text: I think best when I’m doing, not when I’m planning.

mk3.text: I would rather make a rough version than describe the idea.

dr1.text: I imagine worlds and possibilities more easily than concrete things.

dr2.text: I have a thousand ideas for every one I complete.

dr3.text: I’m inspired by visions, not instructions.

pf1.text: I come alive in front of an audience.

pf2.text: I create by improvising in real-time.

pf3.text: I think through my body and voice.

or1.text: I’m the person who makes sure creative projects actually finish.

or3.text: I love the craft of making someone else’s vision real.

an1.text: I find creativity in patterns — in systems, data, ideas.

an2.text: I enjoy taking something apart to see how it works more than using it.

an3.text: My creativity shows up in the elegance of a solution.

maker.name: The Maker
maker.tagline: Hands first — creates by building real things.
maker.summary: You create with your hands. Tangibles matter: objects, drawings, code, a cooked meal. Your thinking happens through doing. Ideas without prototypes feel unreal to you.
shadow: Can dive in before the idea is ready
maker.affirmation: My hands know. I make to find out what I think.

dreamer.name: The Dreamer
dreamer.tagline: Vision-rich — sees worlds before they exist.
dreamer.summary: Your creative gift is vision. You see possibilities. Worlds appear to you. The work is finding partners who help you ground these visions — Makers, Organisers, Performers — so the ideas take form.
dreamer.affirmation: My visions are real information. I partner so they land in the world.

performer.name: The Performer
performer.tagline: Improviser — creates live, in front of, or with others.
performer.summary: You create in real time. On stage, in conversation, in a workshop. Your body and voice are instruments. The audience/partner is part of the work — your creativity is relational.
shadow: Hard to preserve what you do
performer.affirmation: My medium is the moment. I create with whoever is in the room.

organiser.name: The Organiser
organiser.tagline: Finisher — turns chaos into shipped work.
organiser.summary: You make creative projects actually happen. You take other people’s visions (or your own) and you structure, schedule, execute, deliver. The creative world would mostly never ship without organisers.
organiser.affirmation: My structure is creativity. Without the Organiser, nothing crosses the finish line.

analyser.name: The Analyser
analyser.tagline: Pattern-finder — beauty in systems, code, ideas.
analyser.summary: Your creativity lives in patterns. You find the elegant solution, the clean structure, the satisfying symmetry. Engineers, designers, researchers, strategists — many of the world’s deepest creatives work here.
analyser.affirmation: My creativity is pattern. Elegance is my medium.

spiritual-type.title: Spiritual type
spiritual-type.description: Five ways of relating to the sacred, across all traditions: the Mystic (direct experience), the Ritualist (ceremony), the Seeker (study), the Servant (devotion through action), the Warrior (discipline as path).
whatYouGet: Your path of practice — Mystic / Ritualist / Seeker / Servant / Warrior
Strengths and shadows of your path

ms1.text: I’ve had experiences that felt directly spiritual — not mediated by tradition.

ms2.text: I feel closest to the sacred in silence.

ms3.text: Words feel inadequate for what I mean when I talk about the spiritual.

rt1.text: Ceremony, ritual, and tradition feed me.

rt2.text: I find the sacred in candles, altars, prayers, repeated forms.

rt3.text: I care about doing the practice right, not just vaguely.

sk1.text: I’m drawn to study spiritual texts and traditions.

sk2.text: I want to understand, not just feel.

sk3.text: I change traditions as I grow, without feeling unfaithful.

sv1.text: My spirituality lives in how I treat people.

sv2.text: I feel most aligned when I’m in service to others.

sv3.text: Love-in-action is more real to me than belief.

wr1.text: Discipline and practice — daily meditation, fasting, training — feels sacred.

wr2.text: I pursue spiritual growth the way others pursue athletic training.

wr3.text: An hour of disciplined practice feeds me more than an hour of reading about it.

mystic.name: The Mystic
mystic.tagline: Direct experience — what words cannot hold.
mystic.summary: You have had or deeply want direct experience of the sacred — unmediated by dogma. Silence, nature, plant medicine, meditation, certain love. Your challenge: you can’t explain your experiences to people who haven’t had their own.
shadow: Inability to share what you know
mystic.affirmation: What I know, I know directly. I hold it in silence and share it where it’s welcome.

ritualist.name: The Ritualist
ritualist.tagline: Sacred in form — candles, altars, ceremonies.
ritualist.summary: The forms hold the meaning. Repeated prayer, ritual, ceremony, embodied tradition — these are your home. You know why liturgy exists. You feel the ancestor-chain of people who did this gesture before.
ritualist.affirmation: The forms hold. I make them living, not frozen.

seeker.name: The Seeker
seeker.tagline: Student of traditions — never quite done.
seeker.summary: You study. You read across traditions. You compare, question, collect. Each phase of your life has a different teacher. Your gift: you don’t get trapped in any one box. Your risk: you skim many and land in none.
seeker.affirmation: I study — and I also sit. Reading is not practice. Both matter.

servant.name: The Servant
servant.tagline: Love in action — spirituality is what you do.
servant.summary: Your path is service. Caring for the sick, raising kids, feeding hungry people, tending the dying. You find the sacred in the washing-up and the difficult conversation. You often have no patience for spiritual language — it’s all just love expressed in action.
servant.affirmation: My love is my practice. I receive as fully as I give.

warrior.name: The Warrior
warrior.tagline: Discipline as path — daily practice, no bypass.
warrior.summary: Your path is discipline. Daily sit. Fasting. Training. You understand that spiritual development is not about feelings — it’s about what you do every morning at 5 AM. Your path looks grim to outsiders and is actually joyful to you.
shadow: Forgetting that discipline is a means, not the goal
warrior.affirmation: My discipline is devotion. The practice is the path — and the path is also the love.

common.scoreScale: Average agreement per dimension, out of 5.

jungian-functions.title: Jungian functions
jungian-functions.description: MBTI letters tell you the preference. Jungian functions tell you the *stack* — which mental process you lead with. Sixteen questions to find your dominant function.

ni1.text: I often sense how a situation will end long before the evidence is in.

ni2.text: I get single, clear visions of how things will unfold long-term.

ne1.text: My mind jumps between unrelated ideas and finds connections others miss.

ne2.text: I thrive on brainstorming many possibilities — more than executing one.

si1.text: I remember sensory details (smells, textures, exact phrases) from long ago.

si2.text: I prefer methods that have proven themselves over time.

se1.text: I’m sharp and present in my body — fast reflexes, direct engagement with the physical world.

se2.text: I notice small physical details in a room — the light, a texture, who has moved.

ti1.text: I quietly build logical frameworks in my head and test every claim against them.

ti2.text: An explanation has to be internally consistent before I accept it, no matter who says it.

te1.text: I organise the external world — projects, people, systems — into efficient structures.

te2.text: I judge a plan by whether it gets results, not by how it feels.

fi1.text: My values are deeply felt and non-negotiable, even if I don’t explain them.

fi2.text: I decide what is right for me by how it sits with my conscience, not by what others expect.

fe1.text: I read a group’s emotional weather fast and adjust to keep harmony.

fe2.text: I adjust my tone and words to what the people around me need to hear.

Ni.name: Introverted Intuition (Ni)
Ni.tagline: Inner vision — sees the single thread through the tangle.
Ni.summary: Ni-dominants live in a single internal vision of how things will unfold. You often "just know" where something is heading. INFJs and INTJs lead with Ni.
Ni.affirmation: I see what I see — and I check it against what is actually here.

Ne.name: Extraverted Intuition (Ne)
Ne.tagline: Outer possibility — many threads, all tugging at once.
Ne.summary: Ne sees possibilities everywhere. You jump between ideas, synthesise broad patterns, and think in "what if." ENTPs and ENFPs lead with Ne.
Ne.affirmation: My hundred ideas are real — I choose one and see what it becomes.

Si.name: Introverted Sensing (Si)
Si.tagline: Memory palace — the body of past experience.
Si.summary: Si stores exact sensory detail of what happened before. You learn from "last time I did this" and you trust proven methods. ISTJs and ISFJs lead with Si.
Si.affirmation: I honour what I have learned — and I stay open to what my body hasn’t felt yet.

Se.name: Extraverted Sensing (Se)
Se.tagline: Present moment — sharp, alive, right here.
Se.summary: Se is fully present in the physical now. Sharp reflexes, aesthetic intelligence, performance under pressure. ESTPs and ESFPs lead with Se.
Se.affirmation: I am here now — and I can also plan for a future I won’t feel until it arrives.

Ti.name: Introverted Thinking (Ti)
Ti.tagline: Internal logic — "does this actually make sense?"
Ti.summary: Ti builds private frameworks and tests every claim against them. Truth-seeking through precision. INTPs and ISTPs lead with Ti.
shadow: Refusing to commit until the framework is perfect
Ti.affirmation: My rigour serves truth — and truth does not require everything to be resolved first.

Te.name: Extraverted Thinking (Te)
Te.tagline: Systems — "how do we actually execute this?"
Te.summary: Te organises the external world into efficient structures. Projects ship, teams deliver, and the messy becomes tidy. ENTJs and ESTJs lead with Te.
Te.affirmation: I organise the world toward outcomes — and I slow down when outcomes need something I can’t organise.

Fi.name: Introverted Feeling (Fi)
Fi.summary: Fi is your internal compass of values. You know what is right for you even if you can’t explain it. INFPs and ISFPs lead with Fi.
shadow: Inability to explain your compass to others
Rigidity when your values feel threatened
Fi.affirmation: My values are mine — I walk them into the world without needing everyone to share them.

Fe.name: Extraverted Feeling (Fe)
Fe.tagline: Shared harmony — the emotional weather of the room.
Fe.summary: Fe reads group emotional dynamics fast and works for harmony. Your decisions include everyone’s feelings. ENFJs and ESFJs lead with Fe.
Fe.affirmation: I tend the room — and I remember my own feelings count in the weather too.

love-styles.title: Love styles
love-styles.description: Which of the four Greek love styles you lead with: Eros (passion), Philia (deep friendship), Storge (steady warmth), or Agape (unconditional). One isn’t better — they ask different things of you.
whatYouGet: Which of 4 Greek love styles you lead with

er1.text: When I fall, I fall hard — physical, passionate, consuming.

er2.text: Sensual connection is essential for me to feel loved.

er3.text: Desire — wanting and being wanted — is at the centre of love for me.

ph1.text: I am most drawn to people I can talk with for hours.

ph2.text: I need to respect someone as a person before I can love them as a partner.

ph3.text: Shared values and conversation feed me more than grand romance.

st1.text: Love grows slowly, through familiarity, not lightning strikes.

st2.text: The love I trust most grows out of long familiarity rather than a sudden spark.

st3.text: Comfortable, steady, familiar love is what I actually want.

ag1.text: I love even when I don’t get love back — it’s a choice, not a transaction.

ag2.text: My love is at its best when it expects nothing.

ag3.text: I tend to see the divine or sacred in those I love.

eros.name: Eros
eros.summary: Your love is passionate, embodied, consuming. When you love, you love with your whole body and soul. This is the love of poets and lovers — electric, dangerous, life-giving.
shadow: Shorter-lasting love if not balanced with other styles
eros.affirmation: My fire is a gift — and I tend it for the long road, not just the spark.

philia.name: Philia
philia.summary: Your love is built on respect, conversation, shared values, intellectual partnership. You want to be with someone you genuinely admire and who admires you. This is the love that ages best.
shadow: Keeping relationships "safe" when they need heat
Treating a romantic partner like a friend alone
philia.affirmation: My friendship is the foundation — and I let the fire live alongside it.

storge.name: Storge
storge.tagline: Familiar love — grows slowly, roots deep.
storge.summary: Your love is the love of family, of gradual familiarity, of hearth and home. You tend to fall for people who become familiar to you over time — best friends who slowly become more, neighbours, colleagues.
shadow: Staying too long in what’s familiar
storge.affirmation: My love is the slow warmth — and I remember warmth can still surprise.

agape.name: Agape
agape.summary: Your love does not depend on what you receive. You love as an act of giving, often finding the sacred in your partner. At best this is transcendent; at worst, one-sided.
agape.affirmation: I give love freely — and I also deserve to be loved back.

parenting-style.title: Parenting style
parenting-style.description: Your default Baumrind parenting style — Authoritative, Authoritarian, Permissive, or Neglectful — under stress versus when you’re at your best. What research says about each, and one affirmation to carry.
whatYouGet: Your default style (authoritative / authoritarian / permissive / neglectful)

av1.text: I set firm rules but explain the reasoning behind them.

av2.text: I listen to disagreement and sometimes change my mind.

av3.text: I hold high standards and offer warm support to reach them.

ar1.text: Rules are rules — I shouldn’t have to explain them.

ar3.text: Discipline should be swift and consistent.

pm1.text: I avoid conflict by letting most things slide.

pm2.text: I want to be liked more than I want to be obeyed.

pm3.text: Rules feel like barriers to a good relationship.

ng1.text: I often do not know what the people I am responsible for are dealing with.

ng2.text: I don’t have much energy to follow up on things consistently.

ng3.text: I am usually preoccupied with my own concerns and miss what others need from me.

authoritative.name: Authoritative
authoritative.tagline: High warmth + high structure — research gold standard.
authoritative.summary: You set firm boundaries AND explain them. You listen AND decide. Research consistently names this as the style that produces the most resilient children and high-functioning teams. It’s also the hardest — it requires both warmth and spine.
shadow: Can slip into authoritarian under stress
authoritative.affirmation: I hold the line and I hold the hand. Both at once, because both matter.

authoritarian.name: Authoritarian
authoritarian.tagline: High structure + low warmth — demands obedience.
authoritarian.summary: You set rules and expect compliance. Obedience matters more than understanding. Short-term this produces compliance; long-term it produces kids/teams who either rebel or become anxious pleasers. Works in genuine crisis. Less in daily life.
shadow: Rebellion or fragility in those you raise
authoritarian.affirmation: My firmness is a gift — and I soften it without losing it, because warmth doesn’t weaken the rule.

permissive.name: Permissive
permissive.tagline: High warmth + low structure — avoids conflict.
permissive.summary: You prioritize closeness over rules. You want to be liked. Kids raised this way often struggle with boundaries and self-regulation because no one taught them the boundary from outside.
shadow: Missing structure those you love actually need
Resentment building when you finally have to enforce
permissive.affirmation: My love includes holding the line — saying no is also love.

neglectful.name: Neglectful
neglectful.summary: You are often not fully present — overwhelm, work or your own history take up the room. This pattern has the hardest outcomes of the four, and it is also the one that shifts most when attention returns.
shadow: Deep loneliness in those you raise
Attachment wounds that echo for life
neglectful.affirmation: Being present is the first gift — I show up for myself so I can show up for them.

learning-style.title: Learning style
learning-style.description: Four preferred channels for taking in information — Visual, Auditory, Reading/Writing, Kinesthetic. Twelve questions map your preference. Research does not show that matching teaching to a preferred style improves learning, so treat this as a map of what feels natural, not a prescription.
whatYouGet: How you best take in information

vs1.text: Diagrams, charts, and mind maps help me understand better than text.

vs2.text: I visualise what I read — I have to "see" it to get it.

vs3.text: I remember where I saw something on a page long after.

au1.text: I learn best when I can hear someone explain it.

au2.text: Podcasts and audiobooks stick with me more than reading.

au3.text: I think out loud — talking helps me figure things out.

re1.text: I prefer to read about something rather than be shown.

re2.text: I take detailed written notes to really learn.

ki1.text: I learn best by doing it myself, hands-on.

ki2.text: I fidget, pace, or use my body while thinking.

ki3.text: Trial and error is my preferred way to figure things out.

visual.name: Visual
visual.tagline: You learn through pictures, diagrams, spatial layouts.
visual.summary: You think in pictures. Charts, mind maps, infographics, and spatial arrangements are how you process information. Good notes for you are colour-coded, visual, hierarchical.
shadow: Lose interest in dense plain text
Disoriented when information is purely verbal
visual.affirmation: I think in pictures — I build diagrams of what others explain in sentences.

auditory.name: Auditory
auditory.tagline: You learn through sound, conversation, listening.
auditory.summary: You learn by hearing. Lectures, podcasts, conversation, and thinking-out-loud are your best tools. Reading aloud helps you. Silent rooms slow you down.
auditory.affirmation: I learn through the voice — I read aloud, talk it through, listen carefully.

reading.name: Reading/Writing
reading.summary: Text is your medium. Books, articles, written notes, and essays are how you build understanding. You prefer reading the manual to being shown.
shadow: Slow to trust what is not written down
reading.affirmation: Text is my home — and I also step into the body and the room when the room has something to teach me.

kinesthetic.name: Kinesthetic
kinesthetic.summary: You learn through doing. Experiments, simulations, lab work, building things. You think with your hands. Instructions help; doing it once helps more.
shadow: Sometimes skip necessary foundations to just start
kinesthetic.affirmation: My hands know — I learn by moving, making, failing, and moving again.

empath-hsp.title: Empath or HSP
empath-hsp.description: Empath, Highly Sensitive Person, both, or neither. What each means neurologically — they’re related but not the same — and practical self-care for whichever wiring you have.

em1.text: I feel other people’s emotions in my body as if they were my own.

em2.text: I can walk into a room and feel the emotional charge before anyone speaks.

em3.text: Being around people in pain exhausts me even if I don’t interact much.

hs1.text: Loud sounds, bright lights, strong smells overwhelm me more than most.

hs2.text: I notice subtleties (shifts in tone, small changes in environment) that others miss.

hs3.text: I need more alone time than average to regulate.

bt2.text: I need downtime after busy environments to recover fully.

bt3.text: Stories of other people’s suffering can colour my whole day.

nn1.text: Loud, crowded, intense situations energise me.

nn2.text: I do not pick up on other people’s moods until they tell me.

nn3.text: I can take a lot of sensory input without needing recovery time.

empath.name: Empath
empath.tagline: You absorb emotional fields, not just sensory input.
empath.summary: Your core sensitivity is EMOTIONAL. You pick up other people’s feelings and often carry them as your own. This is a gift and a burden. Learning to distinguish "mine" from "theirs" is the practice.
empath.affirmation: I feel what others feel — and I can return what isn’t mine.

hsp.name: Highly Sensitive Person (HSP)
hsp.summary: Your core sensitivity is SENSORY + INFORMATIONAL. You notice subtleties, process deeply, and get overwhelmed by high-stimulation environments. ~20% of people are HSPs. It’s a neurological trait, not a flaw.
hsp.affirmation: My nervous system needs what it needs — I design my life around what actually works for me.

both.name: Both Empath + HSP
both.tagline: Emotional absorption plus deep sensory processing.
both.summary: You have both traits. Emotional fields AND sensory environments hit you hard. This is a rich and demanding combination. Most "I’m so exhausted after parties" people sit here.
shadow: Chronic overwhelm if you don’t actively manage it
both.affirmation: I am built for depth — I protect my rhythm so the depth keeps giving.

neither.name: Neither — Resilient Sensitivity
neither.tagline: You’re relatively resilient to emotional and sensory input.
neither.summary: You’re not highly sensitive in the empath or HSP sense. You handle emotional and sensory intensity well. This doesn’t mean you don’t care — it means you’re not flooded by what floods others.
strengths: Can be a stabiliser for more sensitive people
shadow: Might underestimate what others are handling
Can be dismissive of sensitivity in others
neither.affirmation: My resilience is real — and I respect that others experience more than I feel.

self-compassion.title: Self-Compassion
self-compassion.description: Based on Kristin Neff’s model of self-compassion. Sixteen questions on how you actually treat yourself when you are struggling — and which part of that is the place to practise.

sk1.text: When I fall short, I speak to myself the way I would to someone I love.

sk2.text: When I am struggling, I treat myself as kindly as I would treat a close friend.

sk3.text: In hard times I try to be gentle with myself.

sj1.text: I come down hard on myself for my flaws.

sj2.text: When I notice something I dislike about myself, I feel let down by who I am.

sj3.text: I have little patience with the parts of me I do not like.

ch1.text: When I struggle, I remind myself that struggling is part of being human.

ch2.text: When I fail, I remember that other people fail too.

is1.text: When I am down, it feels like everyone else is doing better than me.

is2.text: When I fail, I feel alone in it.

mn1.text: When a difficult feeling arises, I try to hold it steadily rather than push it away.

mn2.text: When I am upset, I try to step back and see the bigger picture.

mn3.text: I can notice a painful feeling without being carried off by it.

oi1.text: When something goes wrong, I tend to make it bigger than it is.

oi2.text: When I feel low, I fixate on everything that is wrong with my life.

oi3.text: When I am struggling, my feelings run away with me.

low.name: Low self-compassion
low.tagline: The inner voice is mostly a critic right now.
low.summary: When things go wrong you tend to come down hard on yourself, feel alone in it and get carried off by the feeling. That is the most common starting point, and it is learnable: self-compassion is a skill, not a temperament. The component below is where the practice will pay off first.
strengths: High standards — the drive is real
Honest with yourself about what hurts
shadow: Treating a bad moment as evidence about your worth
Isolation when you most need company
low.affirmation: I can hold a high standard and still be on my own side.

moderate.name: Growing self-compassion
moderate.tagline: Kind on some days, hard on others.
moderate.summary: You already treat yourself with some care, and you also still slip into judgment, isolation or over-identification when the pressure rises. Most people live here. The component below is the one pulling your total down — a small, deliberate practice there moves the whole picture.
strengths: Access to kindness when you remember to use it
Willingness to look at how you treat yourself
shadow: Kindness that depends on the day going well
moderate.affirmation: The way I speak to myself is a habit, and habits can change.

high.name: Steady self-compassion
high.tagline: You meet yourself the way you would meet a friend.
high.summary: You speak to yourself kindly when you fall short, you remember that struggling is part of being human, and you can hold a hard feeling without drowning in it. That is a developed skill, not complacency — self-compassion is care plus honesty, and your answers show both.
strengths: A model of self-care for the people around you
shadow: Can tip into letting yourself off too easily — check the standards are still there
Others may read your calm as not caring
high.affirmation: I am on my own side — and I still ask the most of myself.

self-compassion.weakestBody: The component pulling your total down is {{component}}. One small, deliberate practice there moves the whole picture.

mood-screener.title: Mood screener
mood-screener.description: A short self-reflection built around the two PHQ-2 questions used in wellness screenings, plus ten reflections on the same two weeks. Not a diagnosis — if your result is high, please reach out to a professional.

lw1.text: Over the last two weeks, how often have you felt down, depressed or hopeless?

lw2.text: Over the last two weeks, how often have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things?

lw3.text: I have trouble sleeping, or I sleep too much, most nights.

lw4.text: I feel tired or low-energy much of the day.

lw5.text: I’ve been eating much more or much less than usual.

mi1.text: I sometimes feel flat or numb, even about things I usually enjoy.

mi2.text: My concentration is noticeably off lately.

mi3.text: I feel more irritable than usual.

mi4.text: I have stretches of being very self-critical.

lo1.text: Over the last two weeks I have had more good days than difficult ones.

lo2.text: Over the last two weeks I have been able to enjoy small things.

lo3.text: Over the last two weeks I have felt connected to the people around me.

low.name: Low signal — baseline
low.tagline: Most signals suggest you’re doing okay.
low.summary: Your answers suggest you’re largely doing okay lately. The quiz can’t see everything, and "okay" is not the same as "great" — but you’re in a relatively regulated place. Keep tending what’s working.
shadow: Can miss slow drift — check in periodically
Don’t wait until things are bad to tend your wellbeing
low.affirmation: I am mostly okay — and I tend my wellbeing like a garden, not an emergency.

mild.name: Mild signal
mild.tagline: Some low mood is present — worth attending.
mild.summary: Your answers suggest mild symptoms of low mood or low-grade depression. This is very common and is very workable. It does not mean you have a diagnosis. Simple interventions — movement, sunlight, connection, sleep hygiene — often shift this. If it persists past a few weeks, reach out.
strengths: Self-awareness that you’re in a dip
shadow: Trying to power through without addressing
Writing off what good help could do
mild.affirmation: I’m in a dip. I address it gently, with basic care, and I reach out if it doesn’t lift.

moderate.name: Moderate signal
moderate.tagline: Multiple symptoms present — professional support worth considering.
moderate.summary: Several symptoms of sustained low mood show up in your answers. This deserves more attention than self-help alone can give. Consider talking to a therapist, GP, or mental-health service. You are not broken. This is workable and you deserve support.
strengths: Willingness to check in with yourself — that’s real
shadow: Waiting too long to reach out
Self-blame for being in this state
moderate.affirmation: This is a load I don’t have to carry alone. I reach out — today.

seek-support.name: Higher signal — reach out
seek-support.tagline: Strong signals of sustained low mood — please talk to someone.
seek-support.summary: Your answers show strong signals of persistent low mood. This is not a diagnosis, but it is a clear invitation to reach out to professional support — a GP, a therapist or a local mental-health service. The crisis resources below are for right now, if right now is hard.
strengths: Being honest in this screener — that’s strength
shadow: The voice saying "I’m fine, I don’t need help" is often the voice that needs it most
seek-support.affirmation: I reach for real support. I call. I text. I ask. I am worth the reach.

mood-screener.crisis: If you are in crisis right now: in the US, call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline) or text HOME to 741741 (Crisis Text Line). Elsewhere, contact your local emergency number or mental-health service. You are not alone.

anxiety-profile.title: Anxiety profile
anxiety-profile.description: Where anxiety tends to show up in your body and life — somatic (body-first), generalised, social, or performance — and which tools tend to actually help that flavour.
whatYouGet: Where anxiety shows up for you

a1.text: My body carries my anxiety — tight chest, stomach, jaw.

a2.text: I notice physical tension before I notice the thought that triggered it.

a3.text: My mind keeps loops of worry going without a clear subject.

a4.text: I often feel on edge for reasons I cannot name.

a5.text: Being observed or judged by others makes me tense.

a6.text: I avoid social situations more than I would like to.

a7.text: The pressure of a deadline or performance spikes my anxiety.

a8.text: My anxiety spikes most when I am about to be evaluated — a test, a review, a performance.

somatic.name: Body-first anxiety
somatic.tagline: Your body holds it before your mind names it.
somatic.summary: Your anxiety lives in sensation — chest, stomach, throat, jaw. This means somatic tools (breath, walking, cold water, movement) tend to work faster for you than thinking-based tools. Naming the sensation out loud often moves it.
strengths: Quick to notice when something is off
shadow: Overriding body signals until they escalate
somatic.affirmation: My body is the first to know. I listen to it before I override it.

generalized.name: Diffuse, free-floating anxiety
generalized.tagline: It arrives without an address — just background static.
generalized.summary: Your anxiety does not always have a clear trigger. This can be the hardest kind to work with because there is no discrete problem to solve. Daily regulation practices (sleep, sunlight, structured mornings, limited news) often help more than any single conversation.
generalized.affirmation: Not every feeling is a fact. I care for the baseline.

social.name: Social anxiety
social.tagline: The gaze of others is where your system tightens.
social.summary: You feel safer in small, trusted circles than in big crowds or public scrutiny. This is not a flaw — many of the most thoughtful people share this wiring. Gentle, graded exposure plus a pre-planned exit strategy often helps more than forcing yourself through.
shadow: Avoiding opportunity because of the social cost
social.affirmation: I care how I land with others. That care does not have to become fear.

performance.name: Performance anxiety
performance.tagline: Your anxiety rises with the stakes.
performance.summary: You feel tension most when you care about the outcome — presenting, competing, delivering. This is a sign of investment, not weakness. The same adrenaline that fuels the anxiety fuels the performance — reframing it as aliveness rather than threat often shifts things.
strengths: Genuinely engaged with what you do
shadow: Avoiding visibility because of the cost
performance.affirmation: The nerves are proof I care. I channel them — I do not let them drive.

low.name: Low signal today
low.tagline: None of the four patterns is strongly present.
low.summary: None of the four patterns is strongly present right now. Anxiety is a weather system, not a fixed trait, so this is a reading of today rather than of you. If the picture changes, the same four patterns will show you where it has landed.
strengths: A regulated baseline to return to
Room to notice small shifts early
shadow: Quiet can mean numb rather than calm — check how your body feels
A low signal is not a reason to drop the practices that keep it low
low.affirmation: I notice the weather in me without becoming it.

leadership-style.title: Leadership style
leadership-style.description: Your default leadership mode under pressure — Visionary, Servant, Commander, or Coach. Including who you should pair with, and where this style breaks under stress.

l1.text: People follow me because I paint a vivid future they want to be part of.

l2.text: I would rather paint the destination than hand out the step-by-step map.

l3.text: My job as a leader is to remove obstacles so my team can do their best work.

l4.text: I credit my team publicly and absorb blame privately.

l5.text: In a crisis, I expect to make the call and have the team follow.

l6.text: Clear authority and decisive action matter more than wide consultation.

l7.text: I see my people before I see the task they are doing.

l8.text: I get the most joy from watching someone I mentored grow into their next role.

visionary.name: Visionary
visionary.tagline: You lead by naming a future people want to join.
visionary.summary: You galvanize. People work harder for your vision than for any paycheck. Your edge sharpens when you pair with a deeply operational deputy; it dulls when you are expected to manage day-to-day without that partner.
shadow: Moving the vision so often the team loses trust
visionary.affirmation: A vision without an operator is a hallucination. I lead in pairs.

servant.name: Servant
servant.tagline: You lead by removing the obstacles in front of others.
servant.summary: You see leadership as a support role. Your team becomes more capable under you — you multiply, not concentrate. You flourish in cultures that measure team outcomes, not individual heroics. You struggle when you are in a room that only rewards self-promotion.
strengths: Growing people beyond their hiring level
shadow: Taking blame that is not yours
Being invisible in rooms that reward visibility
servant.affirmation: Lifting others is leadership. I also claim what I built.

commander.name: Commander
commander.tagline: You lead by deciding — quickly, clearly, accountably.
commander.summary: You are the person others want in the room when the stakes are high and someone has to call it. Your edge is momentum; your risk is bulldozing. The best commanders mature by learning when to slow down and ask — not just order.
shadow: Cutting off input before it arrives
commander.affirmation: Fast is a muscle. Patience is also a muscle. I train both.

coach.name: Coach
coach.tagline: You lead by developing the person in front of you.
coach.summary: You care about the human before the output — and paradoxically, this produces better output over time. Coaches build the leaders of the next generation. Your risk is under-investing in the task itself; pair with a strong delivery partner who makes the short-term numbers hit.
strengths: Legacy impact — your former reports run things
coach.affirmation: I grow people. I also hold them to what we agreed.

productivity-style.title: Productivity style
productivity-style.description: Your work-rhythm profile — Deep Worker, Sprinter, Connector, or Organiser. Where your energy actually lands, the ideal environment for it, and what to stop forcing.

p1.text: I do my best work in long, uninterrupted blocks — a full morning, not half an hour.

p2.text: Switching between tasks drains me far more than the tasks themselves.

p3.text: I work in intense sprints followed by real recovery — not at steady pace.

p4.text: Deadlines focus me; open-ended time makes me drift.

p5.text: Most of my output happens through conversations with other people.

p6.text: I think best when I am talking, not alone.

p7.text: I feel calmest when my system is tidy — email, calendar, files, tasks.

p8.text: A good system that runs itself is worth more than a burst of effort.

deep-worker.name: Deep Worker
deep-worker.summary: Your output is the output of uninterrupted attention. Protect it — it is the scarce resource in your life. Most knowledge work you do in a 30-minute window would be better done in a 2-hour one.
shadow: Underestimating the value of quick check-ins
deep-worker.affirmation: My deep hours are not optional. I defend them.

sprinter.name: Sprinter
sprinter.tagline: Intensity then recovery. Not steady pace.
sprinter.summary: You move in bursts. 2-3 days flat out, then a day off. You do 60% of your output in 20% of your hours. The mistake is trying to make yourself "consistent" — you are not, and that is not a flaw. Build the cycles you actually need.
strengths: Breakthrough energy when the stakes are real
shadow: Burning out before the recovery arrives
Ignoring maintenance work that requires steadiness
sprinter.affirmation: My rhythm is a cycle, not a line. I honour both halves.

connector.name: Connector
connector.tagline: Your work happens in the room, between people.
connector.summary: You process through conversation. You close deals, align teams, produce ideas through dialogue. Isolated deep work is not your natural habitat — and roles that force it make you feel wrong. You belong in work that rewards the relational surface.
shadow: Avoiding solo work that needs doing
connector.affirmation: Talking is working — when it is the right conversation.

organizer.name: Organizer
organizer.summary: You are calmest when the system is clean. You build the infrastructure others quietly depend on. Your risk is over-polishing the structure and under-shipping the work the structure exists to serve. Make the system; then use it hard.
shadow: Polishing past the point of diminishing return

relationship-readiness.title: Relationship readiness
relationship-readiness.description: Where you are in your readiness for partnership — ready, healing, avoiding, or rushing. Without judgment, with one thing to tend to first.

r1.text: I can name what I want in a partner without hedging.

r2.text: When I see a dealbreaker, I trust myself to walk away.

r3.text: I am still carrying wounds from my last relationship that need tending first.

r4.text: When I imagine dating right now, I notice a tired feeling, not an excited one.

r5.text: I often feel relieved when a date does not go well — I am off the hook.

r6.text: I find reasons to end promising connections before they deepen.

r7.text: I move quickly in new relationships — intensity before knowing.

r8.text: I often commit before I have fully decided the person fits me.

ready.name: Open and grounded
ready.tagline: You are ready — and that is rare.
ready.summary: You know what you want, what you do not want, and you trust your own read. You are in the rare stance where a relationship could be an addition, not a rescue. Be patient — the match you are looking for does not need to be forced.
shadow: Over-filtering from a standard of perfect
Missing warmth because you prioritize certainty
ready.affirmation: I am complete. I choose, rather than settle.

healing.name: Still healing
healing.tagline: Not yet — and that is wisdom.
healing.summary: Something in you still needs tending. That does not disqualify you from connection, but it does mean the work with yourself is the work right now. Rushing into someone else’s life while you are still sorting your own usually costs both people.
shadow: Mistaking a new person for healing
Staying in the wound longer than serves you
healing.affirmation: My healing is not a detour. It is the path.

avoiding.name: Protective distance
avoiding.tagline: You are keeping connection at arm’s length, often for good reasons.
avoiding.summary: You are not wrong to be careful. But notice: are you protecting from a real threat, or from an old story? The risk is building a life so safe it is also hollow. A trusted therapist or friend can often see the shape of it more clearly than you can.
strengths: Self-protective instincts that have kept you safe
avoiding.affirmation: Protection was earned. It does not have to be permanent.

rushing.name: Moving too fast
rushing.summary: You feel the intensity and move quickly — commit early, fall hard. This often reflects a nervous system that calms down when a new relationship is locked in. The work is learning to tolerate the early-stage uncertainty, which is where real knowing happens.
shadow: Committing before fully seeing the person
rushing.affirmation: I slow down at the start. The real fit shows itself in months, not weeks.

wellness-type.title: Wellness type
wellness-type.description: How you best restore — Athlete (move), Healer (deep self-care), Contemplative (stillness), or Balanced (mix). The tools that actually work for your nature, not the trends.

w1.text: I feel best after a hard workout — sweat, muscle fatigue, heart rate.

w2.text: My body wants to be pushed; rest alone does not regulate me.

w3.text: I regulate through slow, restorative things — baths, tea, acupuncture, massage.

w4.text: Skilled, safe touch — a massage, a hand on my back — settles me deeply.

w5.text: Meditation, silence, or prayer is where I actually reset.

w6.text: What I need most in a hard week is solitude, not stimulation.

w7.text: I am at my best with a mix — movement plus stillness plus social.

w8.text: If I lean too far into one practice, another part of me suffers.

athlete.name: The Athlete
athlete.tagline: You regulate through effort — sweat, strength, motion.
athlete.summary: Your nervous system comes online through physical output. Stillness alone does not calm you — you need the heart rate up first. Prioritize hard training as non-negotiable; without it, other tools work less well for you.
athlete.affirmation: Movement is my medicine. I also rest deliberately.

healer.name: The Healer
healer.tagline: You regulate through slow, restorative care.
healer.summary: Your body responds to softness — warmth, slowness, skilled touch. You are often the person others come to when they need rest; make sure you also receive what you give. Book the massage, run the bath, do not feel guilty.
healer.affirmation: Receiving care is not luxury. It is maintenance.

contemplative.name: The Contemplative
contemplative.tagline: You regulate through silence and solitude.
contemplative.summary: Your repair happens inwardly. Social stimulation, even good stimulation, costs you energy; time alone with a practice (meditation, prayer, long walks) is the deepest restoration. Build your life around enough solitude or pay the price in exhaustion.
strengths: Ability to hold complexity without overreacting
shadow: Over-isolating in the name of solitude
Avoiding action by calling it reflection
contemplative.affirmation: Solitude is my nutrition. I also show up for the world.

balanced.name: The Balanced
balanced.tagline: A mix of movement, stillness, and social — all three.
balanced.summary: You are not optimized for any one thing; you need all three. When one is missing, the others cannot compensate. Design a week that includes all three — you will outperform anyone who over-indexes on one.
balanced.affirmation: My balance is my practice. I tend all three legs of the stool.

waxing-gibbous.ritual: Review what you have built this cycle. What one detail, if improved, would change the whole?

full.name: Full moon
full.guidance: Harvest what is ripe. Celebrate progress; acknowledge what is now clearly not working. Emotions run high — move slowly.

waning-gibbous.name: Waning gibbous
waning-gibbous.guidance: Share what you learned. Teach, thank, record. This is integration — not striving.
waning-gibbous.ritual: Send one message of thanks to someone who supported you this cycle. Write one lesson in your journal.
